title: Race Condition: When Two Threads Share a Counter
topic: Race condition — two threads incrementing a shared counter can interleave their load-add-store steps so an increment is silently lost; fixing it needs a critical section

beats.narration: Two threads each add one to the same counter. We start at zero, add twice, finish at two — right? Sometimes.

elements.content: One plus one — but not always two.

beats.narration: Each increment is really three steps: load the counter, add one, store it back. If thread one finishes all three before thread two starts, the counter goes from zero to one to two. Perfect.

elements.content: Two thread lanes (T1 amber, T2 rose). T1 plays load/add/store, then T2 plays load/add/store. Counter ticks 0 → 1 → 2.

beats.narration: But the scheduler can interrupt at any point. If thread two loads while thread one is still in the middle of its add, both threads write back the value one. One increment is silently lost.

elements.content: Same two thread lanes, but instructions interleave: T1.load → T2.load → T1.add → T2.add → T1.store → T2.store
Each step lights up in turn; the counter readout updates per store

beats.narration: The three steps need to happen atomically — no thread interrupts another mid-update. We mark them as a critical section: only one thread inside at a time.

elements.content: Same code block, now bracketed by a glowing critical-section frame; T2 is greyed out while T1 is inside
one thread inside at a time — mutual exclusion

beats.narration: Concurrent code is unsafe by default. Wherever two threads touch the same data, you need a critical section — or the answer is sometimes wrong.

elements.content: (every lock is a fence around a critical section)
